newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens unit cuts 1,200 jobs in cost move.
newsitem.headline: Siemens unit cuts 1,200 jobs in cost move.

text.p: German conglomerate Siemens AG said on Thursday employees in its medical technology group agreed to a cost-cutting plan that would eliminate about 1,200 jobs over the next two years
About 600 jobs would be cut through early retirement or severance contracts and another 200 through transfers to other units, Siemens said.

The reductions came as German unemployment rose far more than expected to 4.66 million workers, reaching levels last seen in the Great Depression. Separately, Siemens finance chief Karl-Hermann Baumann told Reuters the company expected further domestic jobs cuts this year.
MT has forecast a loss for the 1996/97 business year and said falling prices for X-ray equipment and other medical machines were forcing it to cut costs.
In addition to reducing the headcount, MT was trying to raise productivity and improve production processes to become more competitive, Siemens said.
